Create a complete, self-contained, single HTML file implementing an animated "neuron growth network" visualization with dat.gui controls. This is a brand new file — generate the full HTML document from scratch with the following EXACT specification:

STRUCTURE
- Single HTML file. `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html>`, `<head>` with `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<title>Neuron Growth Network</title>`, and a `<style>` block. `<body>` containing one `<canvas id="canvas" width="800" height="800"></canvas>` centered in the viewport on a dark background, plus `<script>` blocks.
- Include dat.gui via CDN script tag: `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/dat-gui/0.7.9/dat.gui.min.js"></script>` — this is the ONLY external resource allowed. No other libraries, frameworks, images, fonts, or textures.
- All CSS and JS must be inline in this one file (style tag + script tags), nothing external besides the dat.gui CDN script.

CSS
- html/body: margin 0, height 100%, background `#05070f`, display flex, align-items center, justify-content center, min-height 100vh, overflow hidden, font-family monospace or sans-serif with color `#ffd400` for any text.
- Add a radial background glow behind the canvas using CSS (e.g. body::before or a wrapper div with radial-gradient from `#101a3a` to `#05070f`) to reinforce the dark neon glow atmosphere.
- The canvas itself should have a subtle box-shadow / glow border using `#00e5ff` at low opacity, and `background: #05070f`.
- Style dat.gui panel to fit the neon aesheticsthetic minimally (optional small custom CSS tweaks to `.dg` panel colors using the `#ffd400` accent) but keep dat.gui's default structure intact.

COLOR PALETTE (use exactly these hex values as defaults, referenced as JS variables/constants so GUI can change them at runtime):
- background: '#05070f'
- backgroundGlow: '#101a3a'
- branchColor: '#00e5ff'
- accentColor: '#d6ff00'
- synapseColor: '#ff2bd6'
- pulseColor: '#fff36a'
- uiColor: '#ffd400'
- gridColor: 'rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08)'

DAT.GUI PANEL
Create `const gui = new dat.GUI();` and a plain params object holding all tunable values. Organize into exactly these folders (use `gui.addFolder`):
1. "Growth" folder with controls: neuronCount (int slider e.g. 3-6), growthSpeed (float slider), maxDepth (int slider e.g. 2-10), splitChance (float 0-1 slider), curvature (float slider controlling random angle jitter), maxBranchLength (int/float slider).
2. "Synapses" folder with controls: synapseDistance (float slider, distance threshold for connecting nearby tips), synapseGlow (float slider, shadowBlur strength for synapses).
3. "Pulses" folder with controls: pulseSpeed (float slider), pulseFrequency (float slider, how often new pulses spawn), pulseBrightness (float slider).
4. "Visuals" folder with color controls (use dat.gui `addColor`): backgroundColor, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor — all bound to the params object and hex strings, wired with `.onChange` to update the live rendering variables immediately.
Add three buttons at the top level or in a "Controls"/root section calling: `regenerate()` (button labeled "Regenerate Network"), `clearCanvas()` (button labeled "Clear Canvas"), and `togglePause()` (button labeled "Pause / Resume"). Implement these as functions on the params object (dat.gui function controls) added via `gui.add(params, 'regenerate')` etc.

SIMULATION LOGIC (organize the JS into clearly commented sections: SETUP, GUI SETUP, NEURON GROWTH, SYNAPSE DETECTION, PULSE ANIMATION, RENDERING)
- On load and on "regenerate", create 3–6 seed neurons (count = params.neuronCount) at randomized positions near the canvas center (400,400), each with a random initial angle.
- Each neuron is the root of a recursive branch structure. A branch is an object with: start point {x,y}, end point {x,y}, a control point (for a quadratic curve, to create organic curving), angle, depth, thickness (randomly varied slightly e.g. 1-3px), and a growth progress value (0 to 1) so it animates growing over time rather than appearing instantly.
- Each animation frame (via requestAnimationFrame), grow branches incrementally: increase each active branch's progress by params.growthSpeed * deltaTime (or a fixed small increment scaled by growthSpeed) until it reaches 1 (fully grown), then decide whether to spawn 1-2 child branches at the tip: continue the main branch direction with slight random angle jitter scaled by params.curvature, and with probability params.splitChance spawn an additional smaller side branch at a more divergent angle. Stop spawning children once depth >= params.maxDepth or branch length would exceed params.maxBranchLength, or once a global max branch count safety cap is reached (e.g. a few hundred) to keep performance stable.
- Use quadratic Bezier (`ctx.quadraticCurveTo`) for smooth organic curves when drawing each branch, using the branch's control point offset perpendicular to its direction by a small random amount for organic wiggle.
- Track all branch tip endpoints. SYNAPSE DETECTION: periodically (e.g. every N frames) check pairs of *fully grown* branch tips from different neurons/branches; if distance between tips < params.synapseDistance, create a synapse connection object {a: branchA, b: branchB} — but first check a Set/lookup keyed by branch ids (or an array scan) to prevent creating duplicate synapses between the same pair.
- Once total branch count stabilizes (growth queue empty or max reached), stop spawning new branches (growth phase ends) but keep the network object alive in memory (arrays of neurons/branches/synapses persist).
- PULSE ANIMATION: after growth settles (or even during), spawn pulses on random existing synapses at a rate controlled by params.pulseFrequency. A pulse is an object with a reference to a synapse, a t value from 0→1 interpolated over time at a speed controlled by params.pulseSpeed, computed position via linear or quadratic interpolation between the synapse's two endpoint branch tips. Remove pulses once t reaches 1. Continuously keep spawning random new pulses on random paths so the scene stays alive indefinitely even after growth ends.

RENDERING
- Clear canvas each frame with the background color (params-controlled), optionally leaving a very faint trail (low-alpha fill) for subtle motion smoothing — but keep it simple/cheap.
- Draw a very subtle static or slowly animated scanline/grid pattern using thin horizontal lines with color `gridColor` (rgba(0,229,255,0.08)) at low opacity — cheap canvas-only effect, no images.
- Draw branches as thin glowing neon lines: `ctx.strokeStyle` alternating mostly branchColor with some branches using accentColor (e.g. every few branches or side-branches use accentColor for variety), `ctx.lineWidth` = branch thickness, `ctx.shadowBlur` set to a moderate value (e.g. 8-15) and `ctx.shadowColor` = same stroke color for neon glow bloom, only grow the drawn portion of the branch's curve according to its progress (0..1) for the animated growth effect.
- Draw synapses as small glowing circles/short glow bursts at their tip midpoints using synapseColor with shadowBlur = params.synapseGlow (brighter/stronger glow than branches), with a soft pulsing alpha over time (e.g. sine wave based on elapsed time) for a "breathing" glow.
- Draw pulses as small bright moving dots/sparks using pulseColor, shadowBlur scaled by params.pulseBrightness, positioned via interpolation along their synapse path each frame.
- Add a faint vignette overlay: a radial gradient drawn last from transparent center to semi-transparent dark (`#05070f`) at the canvas edges/corners, purely via canvas gradient (no images).
- Use `requestAnimationFrame` loop with delta-time based updates; respect a `paused` flag that freezes all updates (but the RAF loop can still keep running or be cancelled — either is fine as long as pause/resume works correctly via the button).

CODE QUALITY
- Keep the whole thing compact but readable; use short section-header comments like `// ---- SETUP ----`, `// ---- GUI SETUP ----`, `// ---- NEURON GROWTH ----`, `// ---- SYNAPSE DETECTION ----`, `// ---- PULSE ANIMATION ----`, `// ---- RENDERING ----`.
- Do not reference any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style anywhere in code, comments, or the title — keep naming purely technical/scientific (neurons, branches, synapses, pulses, network).
- No external assets, images, fonts, or additional libraries besides the single dat.gui CDN script tag.
- Ensure the canvas is exactly 800x800 and centered.
- Make sure the "Clear Canvas" button empties all neurons/branches/synapses/pulses arrays and clears the drawing (network stays empty until Regenerate is pressed). "Regenerate Network" resets everything and starts fresh growth. "Pause/Resume" toggles the paused state and updates its own button behavior (dat.gui function buttons can't change label easily, so a console.log or on-screen text change is optional but not required).
"}
